study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Tabbal et al., npj Parkinson's Disease, 2025
study_identification_part.si4_title: Characterizing the heterogeneity of neurodegenerative diseases through EEG normative modeling

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: This study uses electroencephalography (EEG) and normative modeling to investigate the neurophysiological mechanisms underlying the heterogeneity of Parkinson's disease (PD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD). The primary aims are to chart the lifespan trajectory of standard EEG features in healthy controls over 40 and to map the heterogeneity within AD and PD groups using individual-level deviations from the norm.

EEG signals were segmented into 10-s epochs... and the Autoreject toolbox was used to detect and clean or reject bad epochs.

rci11_site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Site was empirically selected as a covariate (either fixed or random effect) in the GAMLSS models by comparing models with and without the site term based on BIC scores. A leave-one-study-out (LOSO) analysis was also performed to validate model robustness against the influence of individual datasets.
rci11_site_effect_handling_detail.reason: The paper describes the process for including site as a covariate but does not state the final decision (i.e., if it was included and as what type of effect) in the final models presented in the supplement. The LOSO analysis is a sensitivity analysis, not a direct harmonization method.
rci11_site_effect_handling_detail.supporting_text: Model covariates beyond age, including sex and site (considered both as a fixedeffect and a random effect), are empirically selected... The model with the lowest BIC score is chosen, determining whether the covariates are retained in the final model... To validate the robustness of the model, we conducted a series of leaveone-study-out analyses.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Z-score (quantile randomized residuals); Extreme Deviations Index (EDI)
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The paper defines deviation scores as z-scores and defines extreme deviation as |z-score| > 2. It also introduces a new metric, EDI, for clinical correlation.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: This process enables us togenerate the individual centiles and calculate the deviation scores (z-scores) using the quantile randomizedresiduals approach... An extreme deviation is defined as |z-score| > 2... we used the patient-specific deviations to compute a new metric called EDI (extreme deviations index) defined as the averaged EEG source connectivity of the extremely deviated solutions.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Spearman's correlation was used to test the association between the patient-specific 'Extreme Deviations Index' (EDI) and clinical assessment scores (UPDRS for PD, MMSE for PD and AD). Group differences in deviation overlap maps were assessed using group-based permutation tests with FDR correction.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Normative modeling of EEG data reveals significant, heterogeneous deviations in brain function for PD and AD patients, and these patient-specific deviations correlate with clinical severity, suggesting their potential as individualized biomarkers.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study established normative aging trajectories for EEG spectral power and source connectivity in adults over 40. When applied to patients, it revealed high heterogeneity: while only ~30% of patients showed spectral deviations, ~80% showed connectivity deviations, with low spatial overlap (max 25% for connectivity). A patient-specific 'Extreme Deviations Index' (EDI) was derived, which showed significant correlations with clinical scores: EDI correlated with UPDRS in PD patients (ρ = 0.24, p = 0.025) and with MMSE in AD patients (ρ = -0.26, p = 0.01), indicating that greater neurophysiological deviation is linked to worse clinical outcomes.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study proposes that patient-specific deviation scores from normative models could serve as biomarkers to quantify individual variability, moving beyond traditional case-control approaches. These markers show a link to clinical severity, representing a preliminary step towards developing objective, personalized assessments for diagnosis and treatment in neurodegenerative diseases like PD and AD.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Limitations include a sample size that is large for EEG but not on the scale of MRI studies, with an uneven age distribution (lack of data >72 years). Data was aggregated from 14 unharmonized studies using different EEG systems, requiring downsampling to the lowest channel count (19) for scalp analysis. The study did not use biomarker-confirmed diagnoses (based on clinical criteria), did not fully account for medication effects (though exploratory analysis was done), and did not include environmental factors as covariates.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The full list of the 14 datasets used is: AHEPAAD, TUMCP, BASEL, UNMPD, CREAPARK, turkeyAD, turkeyPDAD, lebAD2017, lebAD2019, UMHC, UHTPD, WCHC, SRM, DIH. The study notes that some datasets included patients with MCI, but the distribution was not always clear, so the analysis was not stratified by disease stage.
